# Comments that are really code

Read this before deleting anything. These look like comments but change how a compiler, linter, type
checker, bundler, test runner or packager behaves. Deleting one turns a gate red or, worse, changes
runtime or build output silently. When unsure whether a line is a directive, keep it and let the gate
decide.

## By ecosystem

| Ecosystem | Directive comments to keep |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| TypeScript / JavaScript | `// @ts-expect-error`, `// @ts-ignore`, `// @ts-nocheck`, `// @ts-check`, `/// <reference ... />`, `// eslint-disable*`, `// prettier-ignore`, `// biome-ignore`, `/* istanbul ignore */`, `/* c8 ignore */`, `// @flow`, `/* @vite-ignore */`, `/* webpackChunkName: ... */` and other bundler magic comments, `/*#__PURE__*/` and `/* @__PURE__ */` (tree-shaking), `/** @jsx ... */` pragmas, `// @refresh reset`, `//# sourceMappingURL=` |
| Python | `# type: ignore`, `# type: ...` annotations, `# noqa`, `# pylint: disable=...`, `# mypy: ...`, `# pyright: ...`, `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on`, `# isort: skip`, `# nosec`, `# pragma: no cover`, `# -*- coding: ... -*-`, shebang `#!`, docstrings holding doctests (`>>>`) |
| Go | `//go:build`, `// +build`, `//go:generate`, `//go:embed`, `//go:linkname`, `//go:noinline` and other `//go:` pragmas (no space after `//`), `//nolint`, `// Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.`, cgo preamble comments directly above `import "C"` |
| Rust | `///` and `//!` on public items feed rustdoc and doctests (code blocks in them run as tests) |
| C# / .NET | `#pragma warning disable/restore`, `#nullable`, `#region` / `#endregion` (only if the team uses them), `///` XML docs when `GenerateDocumentationFile` is on (removal can raise CS1591 as an error), `// <auto-generated/>`, `// ReSharper disable ...` |
| Java / Kotlin | `//noinspection`, `// NOSONAR`, `// CHECKSTYLE:OFF/ON`, `@formatter:off/on`, Javadoc / KDoc on published APIs |
| C / C++ | `// NOLINT`, `// NOLINTNEXTLINE`, `/* fallthrough */` and `// FALLTHROUGH` (silences `-Wimplicit-fallthrough`), `// clang-format off/on`, `// IWYU pragma: ...`, `/* lint ... */` |
| Ruby | `# frozen_string_literal: true` (changes runtime semantics), `# rubocop:disable/enable`, `# encoding:`, `# typed:` (Sorbet), `# :nocov:` |
| PHP | `// phpcs:ignore`, `@phpstan-ignore*`, `@psalm-suppress`, annotations in docblocks that frameworks read (`@Route`, `@ORM\...`) |
| Swift | `// swiftlint:disable*`, `// MARK:` only if the team uses it for Xcode navigation |
| Shell | shebang `#!`, `# shellcheck disable=...` |
| SQL / migrations | hints such as `/*+ INDEX(...) */` (optimizer hints are behavior), tool markers like `-- +goose Up`, `-- migrate:up`, `--liquibase formatted sql` |
| HTML / templates / Markdown | `<!-- prettier-ignore -->`, `<!-- markdownlint-disable -->`, conditional comments, `<!-- TOC -->` markers a generator rewrites, template engine comments that hold control flow |
| YAML / config | `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...`, `# shellcheck`, Renovate / Dependabot markers, `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` at the top of a Dockerfile, `# escape=` parser directive |
| Any | license / SPDX / copyright headers, generated-file markers ("DO NOT EDIT", "auto-generated"), coverage pragmas, region markers that a code generator rewrites between, `TODO(owner)` / `FIXME` lines the project tracks with a tool |

## Directives for a tool the repo does not use

A directive for a tool with no config in the repo (an `eslint-disable` with no ESLint config, a
`# type: ignore` with no type checker) does nothing today. Keep it anyway: removing it is a tooling
decision, not comment noise, and it becomes live again the day the tool is added. List it under
"Noted, not done" in the report so the user can decide.

## Doc comments that feed outputs

Doc comments on a public or exported API often build published docs, IDE hover text, or OpenAPI /
Swagger specs (for example decorators or XML docs read by a spec generator). Treat them as product
surface: tighten wording that just echoes the signature, but do not delete them on a public API
without asking. Private helpers with signature-echo doc blocks are fair game.

## Generated files

Skip files marked generated (`DO NOT EDIT`, `<auto-generated>`, files under a `generated/` or `gen/`
folder, lockfiles, vendored code). The next generator run puts the comments back.
